messages.content: Give a skeptical algorithmic review (under 450 words), not a novelty score. We implemented an agent that searches physical measurement programs in DiscoveryWorld Reactor Lab. Public references have known target frequencies; targets do not. It detects varying instrument channels by repeated public reads, tries moving each reference to public locations, measures repeatedly, and considers min/mean/median/max reductions and sample counts 1/8/32. It fits symbolic laws to references and ranks by coefficient-description length, then execution cost. Selection is frozen before target outcomes. Strong supplied isolation+minimum baseline recovers noisy cases. First learned selector solved 2/4 fresh worlds, same as raw model fitting, versus 3/4 supplied calibration; it overfits lucky single reads. Adding 32 fresh reference readings and rejecting programs whose law fails independent repeats is now being tested. This is not yet a novel algorithm. Direct priors: Causal Curiosity (ICML2021) learns actions to isolate factors using description-length ideas; MDA (2026) jointly discovers models and designs experiments, including selecting observation likelihoods/summaries. We need ONE genuinely different executable learning operator, beyond cross-validation, calibration, generic program synthesis, information gain, latent-state filtering or prototype retrieval, that could be motivated by these failures. State exact inputs, update equation/computation, downstream decision difference from the strongest existing algorithm, and one short native-task falsification test. If you cannot identify a non-equivalence, say so rather than rename a standard method. Do not assume hidden simulator parameters or a hand-authored successful procedure.
